chapter: Fats Waller, Zululand and the ideal band
title: Playing a concert in Zululand
summary: He dedicated a concert to Armstrong, spoke Zulu phrases and discusses integration.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Thank God for that through records you know. Their spirit will never leave. I know that I did, I think I mentioned it to you, I did a concert over in (Quamasha?) in Zululand in South Africa.
Oh yes. But that's not on tape. We were talking about that right after you came in.
Well I dedicated the concert to Louis Armstrong. I just knew enough Zulu. I kept
asking this friend of mine there who was a Zulu you know what to say and then I'd say it.
Well just that I was happy to be there and...
Do you remember the Zulu that you used?
No, I can't remember the words. I can't remember the words now.
They were memorized for the occasion.
Yes, that's all. Just for the occasion and that I dedicated my concert to my dear friend, Louis Armstrong, Satchmo'. And well, I believe in that you know. In getting a rapport with my audience.
Now when were you in Zululand?
Now did you take your own group over? Under what circumstances did you go?
No, I went by myself and used local musicians. But we're trying to, the blacks, I can't think of his name, it's a rough name, it's a Zulu

name and they're very hard. I have his address and everything written down there. We are trying to make the integration thing work because there are a lot of people over there who want integration musically you know. Performers and they don't allow that over there. However, we are going to try to break it to get permission from the government to do that.
I mean, that's the only way you can do these things is by trying, give it the effort.
If you were invited by this particular man.

Oh not this one, no. He was the one that booked me at this (Gwamasha?) which is black territory you know, their town. Yes, in South Africa. But they were just marvellous people. Just beautiful people and gosh I really enjoyed that.
